ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

4. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

5. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

6. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. run

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

8. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

9. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. goes

11. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

13. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

14. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

15. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
